title: EU Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content

sources.title: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content, final version (10 June 2026)
European Commission, FAQ: Signing the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content

rules.title: Digitally signed, time-stamped metadata on every output
rules.summary: Record in the file's metadata that the content is AI-generated, digitally signed and time-stamped, wherever the format carries metadata (images, video, audio, containerised text). The Code names no standard; C2PA Content Credentials are the established one. Binding if you signed the Code; otherwise it is what an authority will regard as adequate.
rules.quote: All recorded information will be digitally signed and time-stamped

rules.title: An imperceptible watermark as well
rules.summary: Mark AI-generated content with an imperceptible watermark too, because no single technique suffices. Text needs one only when it is free-form and longer than 200 tokens.
rules.quote: Signatories will ensure that AI-generated or manipulated content is marked with an imperceptible watermark, with the exception of very short text

rules.title: Keep the marks already on your inputs
rules.summary: Make best efforts to preserve metadata marks on input data and on content your system generates or edits.
rules.quote: Signatories will make best efforts to preserve metadata markings on input data and content generated or manipulated by their AI system

rules.title: A detection solution for your own outputs
rules.summary: Make a way available for others to check whether content came from your system: a public specification, software, or an API. It is first-party: it detects your outputs, not anyone else's.
rules.quote: Signatories will make available a detection solution, composed of one or more detection mechanisms

rules.title: Interoperable detection by 2 February 2027
rules.summary: Make your detection reachable in an interoperable way: either a public industry-standard access method that routes detection queries to it, or a publicly readable signpost in the content saying which detection solution to use.
rules.quote: Signatories will implement an interoperability solution for their detection mechanisms by 2 February 2027

changelog: 2026.10.12: first version, from /law/eu-code-of-practice as read 12 October 2026. Rules bind signatories; for everyone else they describe what the Commission found adequate.
